_doc: PIMSA architecture instance A = <M, B, P, C> for Samsung HBM-PIM as modeled by PIMSimulator, following the paper (Sec. 3.1, Table 2), with the timing parameters of the cost models. Every value cites its source in Samsung PIMSimulator (https://github.com/SAITPublic/PIMSimulator).
name: HBM2-PIM (PIMSimulator, pseudo-channel mode)

L_D.src: paper: the banks are level 3; the row buffer of each bank is the node below it (level 4)

I.src: |I_l| per level: 64 pseudo-channels (system_hbm_64ch.ini NUM_CHANS); 8 bank pairs x 2 banks = 16 banks per pseudo-channel (ini/HBM2_samsung_2M_16B_x64.ini NUM_BANKS, one PIM block per bank pair, ini NUM_PIM_BLOCKS = 8); one row buffer per bank

ranks_per_channel.src: derived by MemorySystem.cpp: TOTAL_STORAGE / per-rank storage = (256*64*2 MB / 64 ch) / (NUM_ROWS*NUM_COLS*NUM_BANKS*DEVICE_WIDTH bits) = 2; the kernels use rank 0 only (PIMKernel(mem, 64, 1)), rank 1 is only refreshed

reserved_bit.src: PIMRank.h isReservedRA: row & (1 << 13); reserved rows never reach the DRAM array

register_row.src: PIMKernel.h pim_reg_ra_ = 0x3fff; PIMRank::writeHab: col 0x0 control, 0x1 SRF, 0x4-0x7 CRF, 0x8-0xf GRF_A, 0x18-0x1f GRF_B

B._doc: No software-managed SRAM. The open DRAM row buffer is the modeled buffer, one node below each bank: j = L = 4, B = 1, BSize = one row.

k.src: one PIM block per bank pair (ini NUM_PIM_BLOCKS = 8 per pseudo-channel of 16 banks)

P.src: one PIM block per bank-pair node

R.src: PIMKernel.h num_grfA_ = num_grfB_ = 8: two register files of 8 entries, each paired with one bank of the pair

C._doc: PU control region: the subtree of one pseudo-channel, with the P_C = P * |I_2| = 8 PIM blocks of its bank pairs.

k_C.src: each pseudo-channel has its own memory controller and command bus (system_hbm_64ch.ini), which issue every access to its banks

issuer.src: PIMRank::doPIM: every data-row column command in HAB_PIM mode executes one CRF instruction on all PIM blocks of the channel; the PIM blocks issue no access of their own

coord.src: all-bank mode (ABMR): one column command is broadcast to the PIM blocks of every bank pair; a parallel region over PIM blocks is one command stream

exec._doc: How PIMSA-IR runs on this target, read by metric extraction and by the command lowering (pim_model/pimsa_ir). Program statements say what moves where; these entries say which DRAM commands that becomes.

memory_operands.src: CRF operands EVEN_BANK/ODD_BANK: an instruction reads or writes the bank column addressed by the triggering command

transaction_bytes.src: M.bytes_per_column_access: one column command moves one 32 B burst

broadcast_address.src: PIMKernel.cpp computeAddOrMul/computeGemv: all-bank commands address bank group 0, bank = even (0) or odd (1)

register_file.src: PIMRank::writeHab: GRF_A at register-row col 0x8-0xf, GRF_B at 0x18-0x1f; PIMKernel.cpp computeGemv writes GRF_A at (bg 0, bank 1, pim_reg_ra_, 0x8 + gidx)

crf.src: PIMKernel.cpp programCrf: up to 4 bursts of 8 instructions, written to (bg 0, bank 1, pim_reg_ra_, 0x4 + i)

protocol._doc: Command templates the target issues around a kernel (launch) and around each execution of a parallel region (PC reset). Each step is a barrier, a list of column commands to a reserved row, or the CRF program. Banks are [bank_group, bank].
protocol.src: PIMKernel.cpp parkIn/parkOut (bank index outer, bank group inner, barrier before and after), changePIMMode (SB->HAB: ABMR to (0,0),(0,1),(2,0),(2,1); HAB->HAB_PIM and back: control word at register-row col 0; HAB->SB: SBMR to (0,0),(0,1)), programCrf; executeEltwise/executeGemv issue parkIn, SB->HAB, programCrf once, HAB->HAB_PIM / HAB_PIM->HAB around each compute phase, then HAB->SB, parkOut

kernel_constants._doc: Values the frontend leaves symbolic because PIMKernel reads them from config at run time.
